title: Clarification needed on "check if COOP values require a browsing context group switch" algorithm

labels.name: topic: cross-origin-opener-policy
labels.description: Issues and ideas around the new "inverse of rel=noopener" header

body:
I am working on COOP support in WebKit and would like clarification on the "check if COOP values require a browsing context group switch" algorithm in the HTML specification:
- https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/origin.html#check-browsing-context-group-switch-coop-value

I tried to implement the algorithm as-is but got WPT test failures on:
- html/cross-origin-opener-policy/iframe-popup-same-origin-allow-popups-to-same-origin-allow-popups.https.html
- html/cross-origin-opener-policy/iframe-popup-same-origin-to-same-origin.https.html

This leads me to believe that either I missed some other part of the spec or that the algorithm is incomplete. I am thus filing an issue hoping to get clarification so I can make progress.

Let's focus on html/cross-origin-opener-policy/iframe-popup-same-origin-to-same-origin.https.html, one of the subtests I am failing is:
`FAIL same-origin with SAME_SITE iframe opening popup via anchor a SAME_SITE with COOP: "same-origin" assert_equals: opener expected false but got true`

I see the following comment in the test:
```
// This document has COOP "same-origin". The popup has COOP "same-origin". Therefore there should
// only be an opener and name if the frameOrigin and popupOrigin are same-origin with this document.
```

So in the case of the subtest I am looking at, we have a top document with COOP "same-origin" and origin A, that has a subframe that has origin B. The subframe tries to open a popup that has COOP "same-origin" and that has origin B. The test seems to expect a browsing context group switch when navigating the popup.

If I look at the algorithm in the spec, I would think that:
- activeDocumentNavigationOrigin is origin B (the subframe's origin)
- activeDocumentCOOPValue is "same-origin" (because top document has this COOP value)
- responseCOOPValue is "same-origin" (popup has COOP "same-origin")
- responseOrigin is Origin B (popup navigates to origin B)
- isInitialAboutBlank is true (popup is navigating from initial about:blank to origin B)

Now I think this would cause us to return false here:
`If the result of matching activeDocumentCOOPValue, activeDocumentNavigationOrigin, responseCOOPValue, and responseOrigin is true, return false.`

because `activeDocumentCOOPValue == responseCOOPValue` and activeDocumentNavigationOrigin is same-origin with responseOrigin.

However, the test is expecting a browsing context group switch, and both Gecko/Blink pass the test so either:
1. The algorithm in the spec is incomplete (adding a same-origin check with the opener seems to fix the tests for e.g.)
2. Or I misunderstood some other part of the spec and I am wrong about what the value of the parameters are (I admit this is probably more likely but I haven't been able to figure it out yet).
